subject: Client SDK resilience patterns & migration guardrails
messages:
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@cardinalpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Client SDK resilience patterns for upcoming endpoint migration

Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re starting the endpoint migration next week and want to make sure our mobile + backend clients follow Redwood-recommended retry/backoff and failover behaviors. Quick list of what we care about:

- Minimize duplicate writes during retries (idempotency)
- Maintain low tail latency for live payments flows
- Graceful degradation if hosted model tier is throttled (fallback to smaller model or cached results)
- Clear instrumentation hooks so our SREs can alert on request spikes

Can you share short examples we can drop in our SDK (golang + iOS) and any migration guardrails? Also: what are typical client timeouts you recommend for tokenization vs generation endpoints?

—Sam
Sam Hayes
Director, Platform Engineering — CardinalPay

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client SDK resilience patterns for upcoming endpoint migration

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a small bundle (kp-sdk-backoff-snippets.zip) with:

- client_backoff.go (golang exponential backoff with jitter + circuit-breaker hook)
- ios_retry.swift (iOS: URLSession wrapper with per-route timeout and retry budget)
- idempotency.md (recommended idempotency-key handling for write APIs)
- sample config (recommended timeouts, retry limits, token caching TTLs)

High-level guidance you can paste into your SDK:

1) Timeouts: 3s connect, 3s initial read for small token calls; 10–20s total for generation depending on maxTokens. If you have streaming enabled, keep lower connect/read timeouts but rely on streaming keep-alives.
2) Retries: safe-to-retry on 429, 503, and grooming 500s (5xx non-idempotent writes require idempotency keys). Use exponential backoff with full jitter, max 4 attempts.
3) Circuit-breaker: open after N failures within a sliding window (suggest 5 failures/30s), fail fast to avoid request piling when service is unhealthy; provide a passive fallback (cached result or smaller model endpoint).
4) Rate-adaptive throttling: client should read X-RateLimit-Remaining & Retry-After headers and adjust concurrency down (reduce in-flight requests by ~25% each time threshold breached).

I'll paste a short golang snippet below for the backoff pattern. Grace/Vivek — flagged you to confirm any infra-specific caveats for Dedicated customers.

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

--- begin snippet (client_backoff.go) ---
// simplified (illustrative) backoff with jitter
func backoffRetry(ctx context.Context, doReq func() (*http.Response, error)) (*http.Response, error) {
    base := 200 * time.Millisecond
    maxBackoff := 5 * time.Second
    attempts := 0
    for {
        attempts++
        resp, err := doReq()
        if err == nil && resp.StatusCode < 500 && resp.StatusCode != 429 {
            return resp, nil
        }
        if attempts >= 4 {
            return resp, fmt.Errorf("max retries")
        }
        // full jitter
        sleep := time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(base))) * (1 << (attempts - 1))
        if sleep > maxBackoff {
            sleep = maxBackoff
        }
        time.Sleep(sleep)
    }
}
--- end snippet ---

Attachments: kp-sdk-backoff-snippets.zip, cardinal-mig-map.xlsx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client SDK resilience patterns for upcoming endpoint migration

Kimberly —

Thanks, this is great. A couple of operational notes to add for CardinalPay:

- For Dedicated customers (like some Cardinal clusters), the per-route SLA means we can recommend slightly tighter retry budgets (max 2 retries) and prioritize failover to a local cache or smaller-variant model instead of repeated retries.
- We'll surface per-token cost delta if they degrade to smaller models during fallback (helpful for product decisions).
- Instrumentation: include request_id and traceparent on every call so our tracing can correlate and show tail latency.

I'll add a one-pager to the migration map with these bullets. Vivek, can you confirm whether the routing headers we added in the latest runtime release are backwards compatible with their SDK?

—Grace

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client SDK resilience patterns for upcoming endpoint migration

Grace —

Confirmed: routing headers (X-Redwood-Region, X-Model-Variant) are additive and backward compatible. If a client doesn't send them, the control plane will apply policy-based routing. A couple of extra guardrails:

- If clients send aggressive concurrency (many parallel streams), the runtime will emit 429 with Retry-After once the per-tenant token budget is saturated. Recommend clients cap concurrency and use a local queue.
- For streaming, we recommend a 60s idle timeout and expect heartbeats. If clients reconnect frequently, we surface a metric (client_reconnect_rate) so you can tune SDK defaults.

Happy to hop on the call with CardinalPay during migration window if they want a live walkthrough.

—Vivek

Sam —

Quick recap / actionable items for your engineers before migration day: 

1) Integrate the provided golang + iOS wrappers for retries (see client_backoff.go & ios_retry.swift).
2) Add idempotency keys to any write paths (payments, webhooks). Use UUID v4; TTL = 24h server-side.
3) Respect 429/Retry-After and implement concurrency backoff (drop concurrency by 25% per breach until < threshold).
4) Add traceparent + request_id headers. We will map these to your Sentry/Datadog traces.
5) Set your generation timeout to 20s default with a per-route override. If you need sub-5s guarantees, switch to a low-latency smaller model endpoint.

Proposed sync: Thu Nov 26, 11:00AM PT — 30m. I'll demo the snippets and we can walk the migration map. Does that work?

Kim
